## `files/`

### `test-special-[case].ts` — special simulation tests

Exercise reconciliation behavior.

### `test-[name].ts` — simulation tests

Exercise the named simulation behavior.

### `[file].ts` — simulation implementation

Export the named simulation behavior.

## `prefixes/`

### `prefix1-[first]/checks.sql` — first-source checks

Validate the first source without loading a full world.

### `prefix2-[second]/checks.sql` — second-source checks

Validate the second source without loading a full world.

### `[name]/world.json` — a standard world

Declare the ordinary world configuration.

## `providers/`

### `[provider]/{provider}-[kind]/checks.sql` — provider checks

Check the named provider operation.

### `[provider]/[name]/world.json` — provider world configuration

Configure a provider world.

### `[provider]/{provider}-test-[case].ts` — provider operation tests

Test the named provider operation.

### `[provider]/{provider}-[kind].ts` — provider operations

Implement the named provider operation.

## `unions/`

### `[notes].md` — simulation design notes

Explain the assumptions shared by simulation logic and its visual presentation.

### `[script].ts` — simulation logic

Keep rendering out of simulation logic.

### `[code].{ts,tsx}` — simulation code

Implement a simulation behavior or its visual presentation.

## `worlds/`

### `[name]-special-checksonly/special.sql` — special arrival checks

Validate arrivals that need additional source reconciliation.

### `[name]-checksonly/checks.sql` — arrival consistency checks

Check arrival timestamps and reject duplicate flight identifiers.

### `[name]-checksonly/[note].md` — check documentation

Explain the checks and the data assumptions they enforce.

### `[world]/world.json` — a simulation world

Describe the world's data sources and arrival schedule.

Every path in this directory must fit the project layout or a documented
repository-specific purpose.

## Working with Espalier

Espalier is the architecture compiler for this repository. It turns structural
rules and `ESPALIER.MD` guidance into this generated document, then checks the
working tree against them. Use it to place new code, discover the constraints on
a path, and catch architectural drift while a change is still small.

`espalier help` prints this CLI version's manual. With no page it lists every
page.

Use this loop:

1. Find the intended path in **Project layout** and read the generated guidance
   in the nearest directory.
2. Run `espalier explain <path>` when you need to understand how a path is
   governed.
3. Inspect creation options with `espalier create <path> help`, then create the
   declared file or complete required directory with `espalier create <path>`.
   A required file without a custom template starts empty.
4. Make the remaining change without working around the declared structure.
5. Run `espalier lint` and follow the rule text attached to each finding.
6. Run `espalier build`, review and include any generated guidance changes,
   then run `espalier build --check` immediately before committing.

Generated guidance files are outputs, not edit targets. When a task explicitly
changes the architecture, update the corresponding `ESPALIER.MD` for guidance
or the structural rule modules for structure, then run `espalier build`.
Otherwise, if the work has no valid place or conflicts with a rule, report the
design gap instead of weakening the espalier. Use `espalier build --force` only
to restore a generated file whose provenance marker was removed; it authorizes
overwriting an unmarked document at a planned output path.
